arms.A_native: u=0 all 64 steps. Also the reference trajectory: per-step theta/m/v stored in CPU memory during the run (<=3.5GB per cell, freed between cells) for distance computations.
arms.C_pulse4_release: u=+0.05 at h=1..4, native afterwards, state retained.
arms.D_transplant: INTERVENTION ARM, clearly labeled as intervention (not a training method): h=1..4 identical to C; after the h=4 optimizer step, overwrite optimizer memory (exp_avg, exp_avg_sq) of every parameter IN PLACE with arm A's post-step-4 values (bitwise copy); theta and optimizer step counter untouched; h>=5 native LR. AdamW step counter is identical across arms at every h (all arms stepped the same number of times from the same checkpoint), so no step-counter ambiguity. Semantics: at h>=5, D differs from C ONLY through (m,v); D differs from A only through theta displacement accumulated during the 4 pulse steps.

lr_native, lr_applied, multiplier, preclip_norm, clip_active, tokens

for lag D=1..16: sum_t <v_t, v_{t+D}>, and the same for the residual after subtracting the w=9 moving-average smooth component
slow-direction persistence: mean_t cos(s_t, s_{t+D}) where s_t is the smooth component of velocity
recordings.persisted_small: all of the above aggregates per cell (few KB per cell); full theta/m/v trajectories are NOT persisted to disk

H1_time_reparameterization.statement: Persistent LR-up benefit = path acceleration: the arm is (approximately) the native trajectory traversed faster; aligning losses by cumulative LR time s(t)=sum_k eta_k collapses the curves.
H1_time_reparameterization.construction: s_A(t) = sum_{k<=t} lr_native(k) from diag; for arm X, s_X(t) = sum_{k<=t} multiplier_k*lr_native(k); s_A^{-1} by monotone linear interpolation (lr>0 so s_A strictly increasing). L̃_X(t) = interp(L_A at s_A^{-1}(s_X(t))).

metrics.alignment_rel_err: ||L_X - L̃_X||_2 / ||L_X - L_A||_2 on the val curve grid (every 4 steps, v_score primary, v_eval secondary), evaluated ONLY on non-clamped indices (accelerated arms run past s_A end; edge-clamped points excluded); H1 supported direction requires alignment_rel_err < 1 (beats same-time baseline) with margin
metrics.pulse_frozen_delta_test: EXACT statement (valid for any native LR schedule): under pure H1, L_C(t) = L_A(s_A^{-1}(s_C(t))) post-release, evaluated with the same clamped-mask rule. DERIVED signature: implied lag l(t)=s_A^{-1}(s_C(t))-t approximately constant post-release (exactly constant only under uniform native LR; CPU-tested). Decay of Delta_C(t)=L_C(t)-L_A(t) toward 0 post-release falsifies pure H1 for the after-effect.

H1_time_reparameterization.decision_rule: SUPPORTED only if alignment_rel_err(B, H=64) < 0.5 in >=5/6 cells AND the pulse frozen-delta test holds (constant implied lag + match) in >=5/6 cells; NOT_SUPPORTED if the pulse delta decays toward zero in >=5/6 cells; else UNRESOLVED/qualitative.

H2_slow_fast_separation.statement: The native trajectory admits a slow-fast split: a smooth drifting component plus a faster residual; we only test whether tau_fast << tau_slow (no equilibrium claim, no stationarity claim).
H2_slow_fast_separation.construction: w=9 moving-average smooth component of theta_t; residual = velocity minus smooth velocity. C_v(D) normalized autocorrelation of residual velocities, D=1..16. tau_fast = first lag with C_v < 1/e (per cell; report None if no crossing). tau_slow = first lag with direction persistence of smooth increments < 1/e (report >=16 as lower bound if no crossing).
H2_slow_fast_separation.decision_rule: SUPPORTED if tau_fast observed (crossing within 16 lags) in >=5/6 cells AND tau_fast < tau_slow/4 (using lower bound 16 when tau_slow does not cross); NOT_SUPPORTED if tau_fast not observed in >=4/6 cells or tau_fast >= tau_slow/2 in >=4/6 cells; else UNRESOLVED. Descriptive curves always reported. Claim ONLY 'tau_fast << tau_slow' or its absence - no quasi-steady state claim beyond what the numbers show.

H3_optimizer_memory_after_effect.statement: The post-release retained benefit of pulse4 (B0: ~9.8% of persistent at H=64) is carried mainly by the optimizer memory (m,v) state, not by the raw theta displacement.
H3_optimizer_memory_after_effect.channel_decomposition: At h>=5, C and D share theta by construction, so L_C - L_A = (L_D - L_A) + (L_C - L_D): L_D - L_A is the theta-displacement channel (native m/v), L_C - L_D is the m/v-memory channel at fixed theta. G_X = L_A - L_X (gain). m/v-channel share = (G_C - G_D)/G_C at H=16 and H=64.
H3_optimizer_memory_after_effect.distance_evidence: d_m^D(t), d_v^D(t) post-release (does the transplanted native memory re-diverge, and how fast); d_theta^D vs d_theta^C.
H3_optimizer_memory_after_effect.decision_rule: SUPPORTED if (G_C - G_D)/G_C > 0.5 at H=64 in >=5/6 cells (m/v channel carries the majority of retained gain); NOT_SUPPORTED if < 0.2 in >=5/6 cells (theta displacement carries it); else MIXED/UNRESOLVED. Also report sign consistency: G_D vs G_C same direction.
